investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Available Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was stuck unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the Pending state and the agent was never provisioned.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry it. Of the 6 total nodes, 4 are ineligible due to node affinity or selector mismatch, leaving only 2 nodes capable of scheduling remote-agent pods. Both of those nodes reported "Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm" at the time of each probe run, and the scheduler found no preemption victims, meaning no lower-priority pods could be evicted to free capacity. The result is that every remote-agent pod was stuck unschedulable for ~145–148 seconds before the eval timed out, producing zero evidence and a hard fail against the expected-output contract. This is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing remote-agent pods or other workloads consuming the same extended resource, leaving no capacity for new pods. Preemption is not possible because no lower-priority victims exist.

Secondary — node affinity or selector misconfiguration causing 4 of 6 nodes to be permanently ineligible: if the affinity rules are overly restrictive or were recently tightened, the effective scheduling pool may have shrunk, concentrating all pressure on the 2 remaining nodes.

Tertiary — cluster under-provisioning: the total kata.peerpods.io/vm quota across the 2 eligible nodes may be too small for the concurrent probe load (3 checks each attempting to create a remote agent within the same ~7-minute window), causing resource contention between the sibling evals themselves.

Lower confidence — a stuck or leaked remote-agent pod from a previous eval run that was not cleaned up may be holding a kata.peerpods.io/vm slot, reducing available capacity below the minimum needed for new scheduling.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl or the cluster API shows that kata.peerpods.io/vm slots are available (not exhausted) on the 2 eligible nodes at the time of the failure, the resource exhaustion hypothesis would be weakened and the cause would shift to a pod spec or API error.

If the remote-agent pod spec's nodeAffinity or nodeSelector does not match the labels on the 2 kata-capable nodes, the root cause would be a misconfiguration rather than capacity exhaustion — this would be shown by the scheduler message changing from 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' to a pure affinity rejection on all 6 nodes.

If a subsequent isolated run of remote-agent-create (with no sibling checks running concurrently) succeeds and produces all required evidence, the root cause would be concurrent scheduling contention between sibling evals rather than a persistent capacity shortage.
If the eval passes cleanly after a cluster node is added or kata.peerpods.io/vm quota is increased, that would confirm capacity exhaustion as the root cause.

If the failure recurs even after all existing kata.peerpods.io/vm-consuming pods are terminated, it would suggest the allocatable quota on the 2 nodes is set to zero or the extended resource is not being advertised correctly by the node device plugin.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval that checks kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. used counts on all cluster nodes before remote-agent probes run, and emits a warning if available slots fall below the number of concurrent remote-agent checks configured.
Add a node-eligibility eval that verifies at least one node matches the remote-agent pod's nodeAffinity and nodeSelector, catching affinity misconfigurations before they cause scheduling failures.
Add a cleanup-verification eval that confirms no remote-agent pods from prior eval runs are still running or pending after the withCleanup handler completes, detecting slot leakage early.

Refine the remote-agent-create eval to capture and emit the Kubernetes scheduler event message as a structured evidence field (e.g., schedulerReason) so future failures surface the exact rejection cause in the evidence object rather than only in the check message.

With no schedulable node, the pod remains Unschedulable for ~145–148 s until the eval times out. This is an infrastructure-layer failure in the production-api Kubernetes cluster's peer-pod VM capacity, not an application code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the evidence; this is an eval-detected degradation.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Available Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was stuck unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the Pending state and the agent was never provisioned.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry it. Of the 6 total nodes, 4 are ineligible due to node affinity or selector mismatch, leaving only 2 nodes capable of scheduling remote-agent pods. Both of those nodes reported "Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm" at the time of each probe run, and the scheduler found no preemption victims, meaning no lower-priority pods could be evicted to free capacity. The result is that every remote-agent pod was stuck unschedulable for ~145–148 seconds before the eval timed out, producing zero evidence and a hard fail against the expected-output contract. This is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing remote-agent pods or other workloads consuming the same extended resource, leaving no capacity for new pods. Preemption is not possible because no lower-priority victims exist.

Secondary — node affinity or selector misconfiguration causing 4 of 6 nodes to be permanently ineligible: if the affinity rules are overly restrictive or were recently tightened, the effective scheduling pool may have shrunk, concentrating all pressure on the 2 remaining nodes.

Tertiary — cluster under-provisioning: the total kata.peerpods.io/vm quota across the 2 eligible nodes may be too small for the concurrent probe load (3 checks each attempting to create a remote agent within the same ~7-minute window), causing resource contention between the sibling evals themselves.

Lower confidence — a stuck or leaked remote-agent pod from a previous eval run that was not cleaned up may be holding a kata.peerpods.io/vm slot, reducing available capacity below the minimum needed for new scheduling.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl or the cluster API shows that kata.peerpods.io/vm slots are available (not exhausted) on the 2 eligible nodes at the time of the failure, the resource exhaustion hypothesis would be weakened and the cause would shift to a pod spec or API error.

If the remote-agent pod spec's nodeAffinity or nodeSelector does not match the labels on the 2 kata-capable nodes, the root cause would be a misconfiguration rather than capacity exhaustion — this would be shown by the scheduler message changing from 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' to a pure affinity rejection on all 6 nodes.

If a subsequent isolated run of remote-agent-create (with no sibling checks running concurrently) succeeds and produces all required evidence, the root cause would be concurrent scheduling contention between sibling evals rather than a persistent capacity shortage.
If the eval passes cleanly after a cluster node is added or kata.peerpods.io/vm quota is increased, that would confirm capacity exhaustion as the root cause.

If the failure recurs even after all existing kata.peerpods.io/vm-consuming pods are terminated, it would suggest the allocatable quota on the 2 nodes is set to zero or the extended resource is not being advertised correctly by the node device plugin.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval that checks kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. used counts on all cluster nodes before remote-agent probes run, and emits a warning if available slots fall below the number of concurrent remote-agent checks configured.
Add a node-eligibility eval that verifies at least one node matches the remote-agent pod's nodeAffinity and nodeSelector, catching affinity misconfigurations before they cause scheduling failures.
Add a cleanup-verification eval that confirms no remote-agent pods from prior eval runs are still running or pending after the withCleanup handler completes, detecting slot leakage early.

Refine the remote-agent-create eval to capture and emit the Kubernetes scheduler event message as a structured evidence field (e.g., schedulerReason) so future failures surface the exact rejection cause in the evidence object rather than only in the check message.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-14T07:02–07:07Z because every pod submitted by the eval runner was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler: 2 of 6 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No preemption path was available. Because the agent pod could never be scheduled, the eval probe never reached the agent creation step, and zero evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) were returned, causing a complete contract gap against the expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots on the 2 nodes that carry that resource label. The remaining 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector, so no schedulable node exists. Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims were found on the 2 eligible nodes. This is an infrastructure-layer capacity constraint, not an application code defect. The failure is localized to the remote-agents eval path in production-api and is confirmed as an eval-level failure; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes: the scheduler message explicitly states 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' on those nodes, meaning the allocatable quota is at or above its limit. Other workloads or a previous eval run may have consumed all available slots without releasing them.

Secondary — leaked or stuck remote-agent pods from prior eval runs holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: if withCleanup in run-status-probes.mjs failed to delete a previous agent pod (e.g., due to a prior probe crash), those pods would continue to hold the resource, leaving none available for new scheduling attempts.

Tertiary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or node label drift: 4 of 6 nodes are excluded entirely by the pod's affinity/selector, meaning the schedulable pool is permanently constrained to 2 nodes. If those 2 nodes were recently cordoned, drained, or had their kata.peerpods.io/vm label removed or reduced, the effective capacity would drop to zero.
Lower probability — cluster-level quota or LimitRange on kata.peerpods.io/vm at the namespace level capping total allocatable slots below current demand.

Audit the remote-agents eval namespace for leaked or stuck pods from prior probe runs that may be holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots; terminate any non-terminal pods that are not actively serving traffic.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If the eval probe re-run succeeds and returns all 5 required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) with message containing 'hello from aura', the scheduling failure was transient and capacity has since recovered.

If kubectl describe on the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-labeled nodes shows available (unallocated) vm slots at the time of the failure, the root cause is not capacity exhaustion but rather a misconfigured node selector or affinity on the pod spec.

If no other pods are found holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots in the namespace, the cause is not leaked pods but rather a hard capacity ceiling (e.g., the nodes only support 1 vm slot each and both were in use by non-eval workloads).

If the 4 affinity-excluded nodes are found to carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm label with available capacity, the node affinity/selector on the pod spec is overly restrictive and is the primary constraint rather than raw capacity.

If a passing run of remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, or remote-agent-runtime is found in run history shortly before this failure, the issue is a sudden capacity drop rather than a persistent misconfiguration.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval check that queries the Kubernetes API for available kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on eligible nodes before attempting remote-agent pod creation, surfacing a capacity warning before the scheduler timeout is hit.

Add an eval that detects leaked remote-agent pods (pods in non-terminal state older than a configurable threshold) in the eval namespace and fails with a descriptive message, enabling early detection of slot exhaustion caused by cleanup failures.

Add a node-pool health eval that verifies at least one node with the kata.peerpods.io/vm label has allocatable capacity above zero, running independently of the agent lifecycle checks so infrastructure capacity issues are surfaced separately from agent behavior issues.

Consider adding a shorter scheduler-timeout variant of remote-agent-create that fails fast (e.g., within 30s) with an explicit Unschedulable diagnosis rather than waiting the full ~148s, reducing mean time to detection for capacity exhaustion events.
